deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page belongs to Grothendieck's 1983-84 notes on 'systèmes de pseudo-droites', i.e. arrangements of pseudolines and the cell complexes they define. He wrote it on the back of recycled computer printout. The recto is an IBM JES2 job banner for a job named CRAY2, dated 17 Aug 1982, with an operator notice about machine downtime on 18 and 20-23 Aug 1982. It has no mathematical content, but it is a material clue that the notes were written on reused Montpellier computing-centre paper.

The handwritten part is purely figural. It is a local study inside a construction that the next page makes explicit: two superposed systems of curves.
- The yellow/green lines are a system L whose vertices and faces are in play. Dark green segments look like edges of an auxiliary or dual graph.
- The red/orange curves (λ, λ', μ, μ') are a second system K or Σ. It is being built or 'rectified' near the vertices and faces of L.

Upper-right figure. A single yellow line runs through a hatched band, presumably a tubular neighbourhood or one side of a 'frontière principale'. It is crossed by four orange X-shaped pairs of curves at a', a, b, b'. Each crossing is thickened in dark green, the segment cut out on the line. This appears to show how the red system meets a given line of L: the red curves come in pairs crossing near the line, giving intervals [a', ...], [a, b], [..., b'] along it.

Lower-left figure. A quadrilateral face of L (yellow, sides numbered (1), (2), (3), (3), the top side being '(3)' or a similar label). At each corner a vertex of L is joined by a dark-green edge to an outer vertex. Around each corner two red curves (λ and λ', or μ and μ') pass, forming a hexagon-like local model. Opposite corners carry λ/λ' and μ/μ' respectively. Tick marks on the sides indicate how many red strands cross each side. This is a model of how the red system should look around a quadrilateral face once it is built vertex by vertex.

Middle pencil sketch. A triangle-shaped configuration with labels λ', λ, y, x', μ, μ'. It seems to be a draft of the same local picture around a triangular cell.

Lower-right figure. The same quadrilateral, with corners x, y, x', y' and surrounding regions I-IV. Red arrows and nested red arcs try to propagate the red curves through the interior of the face. The labels a, b, a', b' match the upper-right figure; x₀ marks a base vertex. Several '?' mark places where the matching is undetermined or a choice must be made. The next page settles this: 'on trouve ... les trois types de [figure] → au choix'. That is, several local models are admissible and one picks one.

Following pages place this inside a broader procedure:
- neighbourhoods built from cocells, convex around K₀;
- tubular neighbourhoods of the D_i in X̃;
- rectification of the system Σ on 'exceptional faces' adjacent to K_{D_i}, keeping the part above the principal boundary δ, with the usual changes near critical points;
- a warning that after the rectification, exceptional lines can no longer be characterized as those containing no vertex of L.

So the page serves a combinatorial-topological construction: a pseudoline-type system adapted to a given arrangement or cell structure, near a face. It is checked case by case on quadrilateral and triangular faces, with sign and orientation conventions (ε₁, ε₂, ±1) fixed on the previous page.
errors: No mathematical claims are written, so nothing can be checked strictly.

The question marks in the lower-right figure show the local matching of red curves through the quadrilateral was unresolved at this stage. The next page resolves it as a free choice among several local types ('au choix').
Any reconstruction of what K, L and Σ are is uncertain from this page alone.

ideas.what: Superposing a second curve system on a pseudoline arrangement and fixing its local models at the vertices and faces of the first (quadrilateral and triangular cells, hexagonal vertex pictures)
ideas.modern_name: Local models for pseudoline arrangements, wiring diagrams and dual cell structures; topological representation of rank-3 oriented matroids
ideas.where_published: Not published. The pseudoline notes (cote 154) are only in the Montpellier archive. Esquisse d'un programme mentions tame topology and real configurations only in passing (unsure whether it addresses pseudolines specifically).

ideas.what: Intersection pattern of red curve pairs with a single line inside a hatched (tubular) neighbourhood, labelled a', a, b, b'
ideas.modern_name: Local cut-and-paste / tubular-neighbourhood modification of an arrangement

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a working sketch of local configurations in an unpublished construction on pseudoline systems, with unresolved choices marked '?'. There is no stated result or new connection here. The only curiosity is archival: it is written on the back of an August 1982 CRAY2 JES2 job printout.
transcription_corrections: Upper-right figure: the labels read left to right as a' (below left, near the first crossing), a (above the second crossing), b (above the third), b' (right end). This is not the order 'a b b' a''.

Lower-left figure: the side labels are (1) on the left side, (2) on the bottom, (3) at the top and (3) (or a similar numeral) on the right side. The top label is near the top-left corner along the upper side.

Lower-right figure: the bottom-left vertex label looks like 'x₀' (possibly 'α₀'). Corner labels x, y, x', y' are at the quadrilateral's corners, and the region labels I (left), II (bottom), III (right), IV (top) are Roman numerals.
The recto printout should be identified as recycled computer paper (IBM JES2 banner, job CRAY2, 17 Aug 82), not as part of the mathematical content.
The page number '116' is pencilled at the lower left.
